newsitem.title: INDIA: India Sterlite down on smelter delay.
newsitem.headline: India Sterlite down on smelter delay.

text.p: Shares of Sterlite Industries fell 6.25 rupees, or 2.52 percent, to 242.0 at the Bombay bourse on Friday on concerns about delay in a state government decision to reopen the firm's smelter plant, traders said.

Sterlite expects a direction in two days from the government of southern Tamil Nadu state on the reopening of its copper smelter, which was closed after allegations of a gas leak, a senior company official said on Friday.
"The chief minister has said that the decision will be taken in two days," K. Ranganathan, general manager (commercial), told Reuters by telephone.
Ranganathan said Sterlite had originally expected a decision on when the smelter could reopen by July 31.
Sterlite last month was asked to shut its operations at the southern port of Tuticorin after suspected gas emissions, which reportedly affected more than 100 workers in a nearby factory.
The company strongly denies the charge. The state government constituted an expert committee to examine the emissions from the plant.
The smelter, with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes, began operations in December, 1996.
Company officials have said the closure is costing the company 25 million rupees ($700,280) daily.
